international.title: Burnham should ‘move on’ from Brexit, says Theresa May, as critics hit out over closer EU ties – UK politics live
international.summary: Issue dominates Sunday broadcast round following Friday’s deals on trade and youth mobility Theresa May ‘aghast’ at Andy Burnham’s talk about rejoining EU European Relations Minister Hamish Falconer on Sky this morning criticised the post from earlier this week, where the US president shared a picture of him embracing Putin under the caption “My Friend”. Falconer said Putin was a “butcher” and “not a friend of the UK”. One area where the UK is absolutely and completely united across the whole political spectrum is standing with Ukraine against Russia’s barbaric, illegal war. So would Vladimir Putin be my friend? No. And he’s not a friend of the UK either.” The Prime Minister speaks to the president regularly, and is in absolutely no way pulling his punches about the strength of feeling that the UK has as a whole about Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. “I’m sad and I’m depressed because you know the world that I grew up in was one in which the United States was a defender of freedom, and I worry that we might be moving into a world where that isn’t the case. It’s a grave mistake. He is not our friend, Putin. He is, as others have said, a murderous dictator and no-one is in any doubt about that. There’ll be young people from Britain going to work in Europe, and study, and live, and there’ll be young people from Europe coming to our country as well. I absolutely believe we can both address the issue of Neets, which I think Alan Milburn did excellently this week, and we can address the issue of young people having the freedom to go and work and live in Europe.
